HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE G.S. SANDHAWALIA
HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE HARPREET KAUR JEEWAN

Present: Mr. Pavan Malik, Advocate, for the petitioner (s).
 Mr. Ankur Mittal, Addl, A.G., Haryana, with  Mr. Saurabh Mago, D.A.G., Haryana.

Mr. Ankur Mittal, Advocate, with  Ms. Kushaldeep Kaur, Mr. Siddharth Arora, and  Ms. Naina Jindal, Advocates, for the HSVP.

G.S.SANDHAWALIA, J. (ORAL)
1.
This order shall dispose of the aforementioned 8 writ petitions as common issue is involved therein.

Pleadings have been extracted from CWP-27929-2018 (Shamsher Singh Malik and others Shamsher Singh Malik & Ors vs State Of Haryana And Ors on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134879819/

sentences.text: 2. The challenge in the present petition is to the notification dated 24.05.2018 whereby the State amendment by way of the Haryana Act No. 21 of 2018, Section 101-A of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Haryana Amendment Act) 2017, (for short the 'Act of 2017') was brought into force giving power to de-notify the land acquired for public purpose under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short the 'Act of 1894') on the grounds of non-viability or non-essentiality.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Haryana Amendment Act) 2017
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, the Act of 2017 was apparently given retrospective effect coming into force on 1st day of January 2014 which would be from the date of enforcement of the Principal Act, 2013 itself.

3. The cause of action of the petitioners is on account of the de-notification which was done regarding the land, which was acquired on 12.08.2009 under Section 4 and on 11.08.2010 under Section 6 of the Act 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:131809-DB CWP-27929-2018 (O&M)
and other connected cases of 1894.
The resultant Award was passed on 06.08.2012 (Annexure P-6).
The acquisition was thus complete under the Act of 1894, which was de-notified, vide notifications 31.03.2017 and 11.04.2017 (Annexures P-11 and P-12, respectively).

The amendment has taken place thereafter and the cause of action thus, regarding the denotification was under Section 101 and not under Section 101-A of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: 4. We have already allowed writ petitions by passing a detailed order on 27.09.2024 in CWP-10259 of 2017 (M Mohammad Mamman vs. State of Haryana and others) disposing of 35 writ petitions and by passing a separate order in CWP-8398-2017 (H Harish Kumar @ Harish Malik vs. State of Haryana and others), disposing of 24 writ petitions.

5. Resultantly, we are of the considered opinion that the petitioners have no cause of action as the said petitions itself have been allowed and secondly, the amendment under Section 101-A of the Act of 2017 does not in any manner effect them.
6. Resultantly, the present petitions are disposed of as having been rendered infructuous.
7.
Pending miscellaneous application (s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

(G.S. SANDHAWALIA)
 JUDGE October 03, 2024 (HARPREET KAUR JEEWAN)
